A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ROS research work. All 15 pages of each version, including figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A.1–A.6, support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ROS experiments on three location-based datasets, including recommendation results, cross-city transfer, ablations, and appendix sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains the original ROS experimental results, including Tables 1–9 and the temperature, supervision-scale, and case-study analyses in the appendices.

M1.justification: The hierarchical spatial SID, three-stage Mobility CoT, spatial-guided reinforcement learning, and inference variants are unchanged. The more specific teacher-model designation does not establish a change to the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use Foursquare-NYC, Foursquare-TKY, and Gowalla-CA, with the same cross-city evaluations, NYC Top-K task, and geographic-cue perturbation scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding experiments: Table 1 retains CoAST, GA-LLM, and the other main baselines; Table 6 retains LLM4POI and GA-LLM; Table 8 retains the same Top-K comparators, including OneLoc.

E3.justification: Data preprocessing, temporal 80%/10%/10% splits, metrics, training budgets, and history-length settings are unchanged. Section 3.1 refines the teacher name from Qwen3-235B to Qwen3-235B-A22B without reporting a different experimental configuration.

E4.justification: Both versions contain the same SID and CoT ablations, geographic-cue perturbations, reward-weight and history-length analyses, and CoT-free comparison. Appendix temperature sweeps, supervision-scale analysis, and the geographic case study are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Section 3.1 in both versions states that inference is run three times and mean scores are reported. There are no changes to run-count disclosure, uncertainty reporting, or statistical testing.

E6.justification: Reported table values, plotted results, and qualitative findings match. For example, Table 1 retains ROS HR@1 scores of 0.4478, 0.3864, and 0.3149 for NYC, TKY, and CA. Cross-city, Top-K, ablation, and appendix results are likewise unchanged.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, SID decomposition, and spatial, hierarchical-correctness, and combined reward definitions in Section 2 and Appendix A.3 are unchanged. No formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims, including over 10% relative hit-rate gains, improved geographic plausibility, and cross-city transfer with a smaller backbone.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and interpretations of the experiments are unchanged. Both versions retain the limitation that the distance-based feasibility prior may underweight realistic rapid long-distance travel through transportation networks.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability footnote on page 1 and identifies the teacher more precisely as Qwen3-235B-A22B in Section 3.1. Appendix A.3 and the remaining implementation details are unchanged; these edits improve documentation without establishing an experimental change.

R1.justification: The cited works, related-work discussion, and positioning relative to existing POI recommendation, generative recommendation, and CoT methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: The affiliation is expanded to include the School of Software Engineering, a code footnote is added, and the teacher-model name is refined. Scientific prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Existing material is reflowed: Figure 4 moves from PDF page 7 to page 8, and the Appendix A.6 heading moves onto page 15 with its prompt examples, whose spacing becomes more compact. Figure content, table structures, captions, and numbering are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 modestly improves documentation through an explicit code-access reference and a more precise teacher-model identifier. Appendix A.6 also presents its heading and examples together more clearly. The scientific methods, evidence, and conclusions remain unchanged, so the overall improvement is limited.
